sections.h2: Dahej ran at 91.9% in April–May 2026; the other seven ran at 10.5–40.1%

chart.title: Dahej runs near full; most other terminals run at a fifth to a half
chart.sub: Terminal utilisation, April–May 2026, % of capacity (PPAC data).

sections.means: Dahej has run near full for a decade, while the other seven have mostly run at a fifth to a half of their capacity.
sections.todo: PNGRB should make registration of any new LNG terminal conditional on booked evacuation pipeline capacity.

sections.h2: Dahej's expansion cost ₹370 crore per MMTPA; new onshore terminals ₹950–1,290 crore

chart.title: Expanding an existing site costs about a third as much per tonne of capacity
chart.sub: Project cost divided by capacity added, ₹ crore per MMTPA, nominal rupees.
chart.source: PNGRB HLEC (Nov 2025); Petronet LNG filings; PTI; press reports.

sections.means: Expansions reuse jetties, land and pipeline connections, which is why they cost about a third as much per tonne of capacity.
sections.todo: Each terminal approval should show capital cost per MMTPA with marine works listed separately, as this piece proposes.

sections.h2: Four new onshore terminals ran 22–35 months late; Dahej's expansion ran 12

chart.title: Each new onshore terminal slipped further than the Dahej expansion did
chart.sub: Months late against the first stated commissioning date.
chart.source: PNGRB HLEC (Nov 2025); company and press reports.

sections.means: The recurring causes are breakwaters, evacuation pipelines not ready at commissioning, and lease or clearance disputes, not tank construction.
sections.todo: Terminals should be measured from board approval to commercial operation and against the first date announced, as this piece proposes.

sections.h2: Gujarat's gas pipelines carry about 40 MMSCMD; its terminals can regasify 95–100

chart.title: Terminal capacity in Gujarat outruns the pipelines that carry gas away
chart.sub: Million standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD).

sections.means: GSPL's high-pressure network ran at 100.5% in 2024-25, so expansions in Gujarat can be limited by the pipes out.
sections.todo: GSPL and PNGRB should publish a funded plan to raise Gujarat's evacuation capacity before Hazira's expansion and Jafrabad are commissioned.
